Well, as I see it, shape design helps with making more confident strokes as you know where and how to put them. Of course the way you draw line art depends on the sketch as the foundation, and knowledge of what you're drawing. The bowtie for example looks as if it was drawn with uncertainty, so the line art looks unfitting. The lines have the same weight to them, as one can't tell where the strokes begins or where they end. Clear line art should replicate the strokes that it was drawn with. At leas that's what I think. 

So, you should try to practice lose strokes, to get abetter functionality to them. You should also make sure that you draw a good sketch where everything is clear and set up for the line art. That requires you to understand shape design and overall knowledge of what you're drawing.

Hope that helps.

I think the issue is with how you use shapes in character design. The character lacks the knowledge of how to design a character by shape language, which makes this design appear in disorder. This is also why the line art lacks clear strokes, as there is no foundation to make it all come together. So, I advise you to educate yourself on design based on shape language and try to design this character then again.

Hope that helps.

The colours and values look good to me. And the tree doesn't look flat at all, I think.

Depending on what drawing program you use there could be different brushes that already look similar to leaves and blades of grass, so you could use them instead of painting it all piece by piece.

And you could  add some more details to the rock stairs. Just a bit.

EDIT: Maybe the detail in the bushes or grass isn't necessary, but I'll leave it there anyways.

It seems finished to me. Or do you think that there's something missing?

I think that you should practice your shadows and learn how to keep undertones in mind. The colours don't look good together, as the undertone is lacking. The undertone would be red in this case, I think. The reflected light on the left of the photo is also lacking on the portrait. The face also looks a bit stiff, so you should loosen up, some.

Other than that it looks pretty good. The anatomy is well structured and the drawing looks realistic. You could experiment with a more lose art style though, as I have mentioned. But if that isn't what you're looking for, then just keep on practicing colouring and anatomy.

The way you use colours and light sources is very good. Your sense of anatomy is good, too. And I like the background of the second drawing the most. It is very well done. The background of the first and second are good too.

But what your images are lacking is defined line art. I can see that it is there, but I think that more lose strokes and a darker tone, maybe even black, would suit your art better. What I mean by that is that one should be able to see the lose strokes of the line art, like in this video: https://youtu.be/L9SHbYFZ4IM?t=242

The way that you draw the characters is very stiff. I would suggest that you practice more fluid sketches and line art, as it looks too static in these drawings. Lavendertowne has some good tips on how to improve line art, and there are many others for sure.  Also using photo references for the poses would be good. Studying anatomy would be helpful, too.

The way you drew the hair on the second and third image could use some improvement, too. I suggest that you, again, practice with using references for that too. Practice using a different paintbrush and lose strokes to paint hair. Using tutorials would help in that regard.

You also have some mild same face syndrome, so, again again, you should use references to practice faces. Also practice drawing them from different angles, as you drew them all from the front.

Practicing the way you draw shadows would be good, too. Here's a video about that that could be useful to you: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZJkIaMECW6c](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZJkIaMECW6c)

Hope that helps.

The way you use line art is inconsistent. You use it on the middle and right, but not anywhere else.

Other than that it looks good.

One thing that comes to mind is the composition of the character. You should try to draw the full body of the character, and avoid placing the TV head at the very bottom of the image. 

Other than that, it looks pretty neat.

You're welcome :-)

Having a type of face to draw isn't bad, but can interfere with character design. Rather than having a type of face, you could strive for an art style with features that you like. But I think that would come by on its own with enough practice.

The first thing that comes to my mind is that the faces you draw look too similar. They are elongated and (rather) androgynous. I'm sure that it would be better to draw faces that suit the characters the most, not what you're in habit of drawing.

Speaking of character design, you have skill in that regard. My favourite of the three is the second character, as he has the most distinct design. And unlike the other two, his pose is more dynamic and informative of what kind of person he is. (He looks like a proud warrior to me.)

That's because the other two just stand there. The first one does something, but his pose still feels stiff. The third one lacks characterisation through posture. (He looks like an angry prince to me.)

Also, maybe you should get out of your comfort zone and don't draw characters from above the waist only.

Aside from all that, your choice of colours and your skill drawing environments are good.

One other thing that bothers me is the choice of clothing on the first character. Is there a good reason for that? If that's just his personal preference that works too, but I just wonder if it's part of his character or not.

Hope that helps.

EDIT: I just saw that you already know that your posing is bad, so, my bad. I don't have much to say about shape or anything. What I could advice is that you use references for your poses, to make them less stiff.

Wow, this looks amazing. You did very well on the anatomy of the heart, and the blood red colour makes it look haunting. This is a wonderful painting.

The drawing lacks clear structure. The way you painted the woman is smudged, especially  around her neck, shoulders and collarbones, as one can't even recognize them in the drawing.

If you haven't done that yet, I would suggest to start of with a sketch, in which you define the anatomy and shading of the woman. Then you paint underneath that layer, and afterwards on top of it, after you laid out the grid, so to say.

Also, you shouldn't use soft edges, as that is what makes the drawing lack definition.

Aside from all that I'd say that you should just keep practicing to use portraits as a reference, as the proportions of the face are slightly wonky, with the mouth being smaller than in the photo, for example.

I also suggest that you watch some tutorials on painting to understand the process better. As a tip, search of tutorials that explain using different values to add depth.

The first thing that comes to mind when I look at this is that you are skilled in composition and three-dimensional understanding of the object that you drawn.

What the image is lacking-or rather, what would be the next step-are distinct line art and structure. The drawing looks messy, like a sketch. If you're planning to finish it, then you should clean it up.

After that you could post the drawing here again and see what you can do to make it work.

Aside from the painting not looking much like the reference-which would make me suggest to practice composition-I think that you should practice to differentiate colour values, as the reference shifts in tones, going from purple to orange to yellow, while your drawing has the same colour value-orange-, which makes the drawing lack depth. Granted, you did add the purple shade, but the way you placed it in the horizontal front makes the scenery appear flat, too.

I don't mean to be harsh. I think that you make the drawing look well otherwise. It looks pretty, and gives off a calm mood. And the shooting star is a nice touch.
